@graph.nrr:outcomeSummary: Alkyne: 0.3 mM/s and 4 % at 60 °C against 9.6 mM/s and 87 % for free BH3; 50 % at 80 °C and 94 % at 100 °C. Alkene: 0.02 mM/s and 3 % at 60 °C against 1.8 mM/s and >95 %; complete at 80 and 100 °C. HBpin alone decomposes to BH3 from 80 °C.
nrr:provenanceNotes: Attempt headline is 'refuted' because the finding the authors built the paper around is the refutation of the inference 'no inhibition means true catalysis' above 60 °C; the six kinetic findings carry the data, two of them informative negatives at 60 °C.
@graph.nrr:successCriteria: Adduct-catalysed rate indistinguishable from the no-catalyst background and far below the Me2S.BH3 control, with less than 5 % product.

nrr:evidence.label: Abstract
nrr:evidence.quote: Kinetic analyses showed that TMEDA inhibition is only applicable below 60 °C and that other amine traps are likewise ineffective.

nrr:evidence.label: Conclusion
nrr:evidence.quote: Application of the TMEDA inhibition test, to identify hidden BH3 catalysis, was found to be unsuitable above 60 °C when using a one-to-one loading of TMEDA to 'catalyst'. Higher loading of TMEDA, with respect to catalyst, offered increased inhibition of BH3 catalysis but did not give complete inhibition of catalysis; thus, false negatives remain possible. Reaction at temperatures of >=80 °C will generate BH3 by thermal decomposition of HBpin, and therefore will always be susceptible to hidden BH3 catalysis.

@graph.nrr:informativenessReason: an affirmative refutation is judged on the refuting analysis, not on the controls of the run it refutes
@graph.nrr:note: What is refuted is the inference 'no inhibition, therefore true catalysis' above 60 °C, not the existence of hidden catalysis. The record keeps the test valid at or below 60 °C.
@graph.nrr:question: Does a lack of inhibition by TMEDA demonstrate true, non-boron catalysis at the temperatures the test is used at?

evidence.label: Abstract
evidence.quote: Kinetic analyses showed that TMEDA inhibition is only applicable below 60 °C and that other amine traps are likewise ineffective.

evidence.label: Conclusion
evidence.quote: Application of the TMEDA inhibition test, to identify hidden BH3 catalysis, was found to be unsuitable above 60 °C when using a one-to-one loading of TMEDA to 'catalyst'. Higher loading of TMEDA, with respect to catalyst, offered increased inhibition of BH3 catalysis but did not give complete inhibition of catalysis; thus, false negatives remain possible. Reaction at temperatures of >=80 °C will generate BH3 by thermal decomposition of HBpin, and therefore will always be susceptible to hidden BH3 catalysis.

findings.informativenessReason: an affirmative refutation is judged on the refuting analysis, not on the controls of the run it refutes
findings.note: What is refuted is the inference 'no inhibition, therefore true catalysis' above 60 °C, not the existence of hidden catalysis. The record keeps the test valid at or below 60 °C.
